title: Reversion, Retention, and Semantic Intervention: Measuring Functional Content in CLIP Fine-Tuning Deltas
abstract: arXiv:2610.34144v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Fine-tuning adapts pretrained models to new tasks, but identifying which weight changes support the resulting behavior remains difficult. Weight-space interpretability assigns semantic descriptions to these changes, called fine-tuning deltas. Such descriptions leave open how much task performance depends on the identified updates, particularly when other updates can support the same predictions. We address this gap by pairing reversion, which restores selected parameters to their pretrained values, with retention, which keeps only selected fine-tuning updates. translated_title: 回退、保留与语义干预：衡量CLIP微调增量中的功能性内容
translated_abstract: 微调使预训练模型能够适应新任务，但识别哪些权重变化支持了最终行为仍然很困难。权重空间可解释性为这些变化赋予语义描述，称为微调增量。然而这类描述并未说明任务性能在多大程度上依赖于所识别的更新，尤其是当其他更新也能支持相同预测时。我们通过将回退（reversion，将选定参数恢复到预训练值）与保留（retention，仅保留选定的微调更新）相结合来填补这一空白。我们使用统一的调优方案（微调最后六个视觉块），在合成金融图表、Flowers102、EuroSAT和FGVCAircraft数据集上用ViT-L/14评估对比语言-图像预训练（CLIP）模型，并在Flowers102上用ViT-B/16进行评估。我们的贡献有三点：首先，仅注意力值输出（VO）更新就能恢复43-87%的准确率提升，尽管……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将“回退”（将选定参数恢复至预训练值）与“保留”（仅保留选定微调更新）两种干预手段相结合，来量化语义上识别出的CLIP微调增量对任务性能的实际功能性贡献，并发现仅注意力值输出（VO）更新即可恢复43-87%的准确率提升。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes pairing reversion (restoring selected parameters to their pretrained values) with retention (keeping only selected fine-tuning updates) to measure the functional contribution of semantically identified CLIP fine-tuning deltas, finding that attention value-output (VO) updates alone recover 43-87% of the accuracy improvement.
